>     secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production",

> **Point 1 : Vérification du montant dans le webhook Dodo**

> - Spec Standard Webhooks : headers `webhook-id`, `webhook-timestamp`, `webhook-signature`
> - signedContent = `${webhook-id}.${webhook-timestamp}.${rawBody}`
> - HMAC-SHA256 hex, comparé avec le contenu de `webhook-signature` (souvent préfixé `v1,`)
> - Le code actuel fait HMAC du body seul et essaie 3 noms de headers. Il faut :
>   - Lire `webhook-signature` (prioritaire), avec fallbacks `dodo-signature`, `x-dodo-signature`, et une variable d'env `DODO_SIGNATURE_HEADER` configurable.
>   - Construire le message signé selon la spec (id.timestamp.body), avec fallback sur body seul si id/timestamp absents (pour compatibilité avec d'anciens webhooks).
>   - Gérer le préfixe `v1,` et comparer en hex (et base64 en fallback).
> 
> **Point 3 : PIN agent (et aussi code d'activation terminal)**
> - Remplacer `?agentPin=${pin}` par un cookie éphémère httpOnly : `sigma_agent_pin` avec le PIN + nom, maxAge court (2 min), path `/events/<eventId>`, consommé à la lecture (la page le lit puis l'efface).
> - Problème : la page événement est un composant serveur ; pour effacer un cookie, on ne peut pas le faire directement dans le render d'un server component (il faut une server action ou un redirect). La façon propre : 
>   - L'action `addAgentAction` pose le cookie (c'est une server action, ok pour `cookies().set`) puis redirige vers `/events/${eventId}?agentAssigned=1` (sans PIN dans l'URL).
>   - La page événement lit le cookie `sigma_agent_pin` et l'affiche une seule fois via un composant client qui appelle une server action `consumeAgentPinAction()` au montage pour effacer le cookie.
>   - En fait, plus simple : un composant client `AgentPinReveal` reçoit pin+name en props (rendus depuis le cookie lu côté serveur), et appelle une server action au montage qui efface le cookie. Ainsi un refresh ne réaffiche pas le PIN.
> - Même traitement pour les codes d'activation terminal (`terminalPin`).
> 
> Attention : `cookies()` est asynchrone en Next 15/16 (`await cookies()`). Déjà utilisé dans lib/auth.ts avec `await cookies()`. OK.
> 
> Vérifions que la page événement peut lire le cookie : `const store = await cookies(); const pinCookie = store.get("sigma_agent_pin")`.
> 
> Le composant client doit appeler la server action qui efface le cookie. Je vais créer `app/actions.ts` : `export async function consumeAgentPinAction()` qui efface les deux cookies (agent + terminal). En fait un seul `consumeRevealCookie` qui efface `sigma_agent_pin` et `sigma_terminal_code`.
> 
> Attention aussi au cookie `path`: si je mets path `/events/${eventId}`, le cookie ne sera envoyé que pour cette page. C'est bien. Mais la page est `/events/[id]` — le path doit être `/events/${eventId}` exactement. Un cookie avec `path=/events/xyz` sera envoyé pour `/events/xyz` et ses sous-chemins. Parfait.
> 
> Je vais créer un helper dans actions.ts ou directement :
> 
> ```ts
> // Secret éphémère affiché une seule fois (PIN agent / code terminal) : stocké
> // dans un cookie httpOnly court au lieu d'un paramètre d'URL (jamais dans
> // l'historique ni les logs serveur).
> const REVEAL_COOKIE = "sigma_agent_pin";  // ou deux cookies
> ```
> 
> Décision : deux cookies `sigma_agent_pin` et `sigma_terminal_code`, posés avec `path: /events/${eventId}`, `maxAge: 120` (2 min), httpOnly, sameSite lax, secure en prod. La page lit le cookie correspondant, affiche le secret une fois, et un composant client efface les cookies au montage.
>

> export function verifyWebhookSignature(
>   rawBody: string,
>   opts: { id?: string | null; timestamp?: string | null; signature?: string | null }
> ): boolean {
>   const secret = process.env.DODO_WEBHOOK_SECRET;
>   const signature = opts.signature;
>   if (!secret || !signature) return false;
>   try {
>     // Spec Standard Webhooks : message signé = id.timestamp.body
>     const signedContent = opts.id && opts.timestamp
>       ? `${opts.id}.${opts.timestamp}.${rawBody}`
>       : rawBody; // fallback body seul (anciens webhooks)
>     const computed = crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret).update(signedContent).digest("hex");
>     // La signature peut être préfixée « v1, » (format svix) ou hex pure
>     const provided = signature.replace(/^v1[,;]?\s*/i, "").trim();

>     const b = Buffer.from(provided, "hex");

>       // Fallback : essayer base64
>       const c = Buffer.from(provided, "base64");
>       if (a.length !== c.length) return false;
>       return crypto.timingSafeEqual(a, c);
>     }
>     return crypto.timingSafeEqual(a, b);
>   } catch {
>     return false;
>   }
> }
> ```

Les autres noms sont des fallbacks\n// pour les anciennes versions / proxys.\nfunction signatureHeader(request: Request): string | null {\n  const configured = process.env.DODO_SIGNATURE_HEADER;\n  const candidates = [\n    configured,\n    \"webhook-signature\",\n    \"dodo-signature\",\n    \"x-dodo-signature\",\n  ].filter(Boolean) as string[];\n  for (const name of candidates) {\n    const value = request.headers.get(name);\n    if (value) return value;\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\n// Webhook Dodo Payments : confirmation du paiement mobile money (HTTPS requis\n// en production — la clé DODO_WEBHOOK_SECRET n'est jamais exposée).\n//\n// Flux réel :\n//   1. /acheter/payer → initiation du paiement chez Dodo (lib/payments.ts)\n//   2. le client paie sur le checkout Dodo (MTN MoMo / Moov / Orange / Celtiis)\n//   3. \"\");\n  // Dodo « payment.succeeded » / « completed » / « success » : paiement réussi.\n  const completed = /complete|success|paid/i.test(status) || String(payload.type ?? \"\").includes(\"succeeded\");\n\n  if (!paymentId) {\n    return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: \"NO_PAYMENT_ID\" }, { status: 400 });\n  }\n\n  const order = await prisma.order.findUnique({\n    where: { externalPaymentId: paymentId },\n    include: { event: true },\n  });\n  if (!order) {\n    // Paiement inconnu : on accuse réception sans confirmer (rien à confirmer).\n    return NextResponse.json({ ok: true, ignored: \"unknown_payment\" });\n  }\n\n  // Événements non-liés au succès (failed, pending…) : on trace le statut et on\n  // répond 200 pour éviter les rejeux inutiles.\n  if (!completed) {\n    await prisma.order.update({\n      where: { id: order.id },\n      data: { externalStatus: status.slice(0, 40) || \"unknown\" },\n    });\n    return NextResponse.json({ ok: true, status });\n  }\n\n  // Paiement déjà confirmé : idempotent (les webhooks sont parfois redélivrés).\n  if (order.status === OrderStatus.PAID) {\n    return NextResponse.json({ ok: true, already: true });\n  }\n\n  // 🔒 Anti-fraude : le montant reçu doit correspondre à la commande\n  // (amount + frais de livraison), en minor units (×100) ou en unités majeures.\n  // Un paiement partiel ou surévalué est refusé — on ne confirme jamais.\n  const expectedFcfa = order.amount + (order.deliveryFee || 0);\n  const receivedRaw = Number(data.total_amount ?? > _Reasoning_
> Now point 3: secure agent PIN (and terminal activation code) display via ephemeral cookie instead of query string.
> 
> The current flow:
> - `addAgentAction` → `redirect(/events/${eventId}?agentPin=${pin}&agentName=...)` 
> - `resetAgentPinAction` → same
> - `createTerminalAction` / `regenerateTerminalCodeAction` → `redirect(/events/${eventId}?terminalPin=${terminal.activationCode}&terminalName=...)`
> 
> The event page reads `sp.agentPin`, `sp.agentName`, `sp.terminalPin`, `sp.terminalName` and displays them.
> 
> The fix: store the one-time secret in an httpOnly ephemeral cookie (short TTL, e.g. 2 min), then redirect without the secret in the URL. The page reads the cookie and displays the PIN once. To ensure "displayed once", the cookie can be consumed/deleted after reading... but a server component can't delete cookies during render (cookies().delete is only allowed in Server Actions / Route Handlers). 
> 
> Approach: 
> 1. In the server action, set cookie `sigma_agent_pin` (httpOnly, sameSite lax, secure in prod, maxAge ~120s, path `/events/<id>` or just `/`) containing the pin + name (JSON encoded or separate fields). Then redirect to `/events/<id>?agentAssigned=1` (no secret).
> 2. In the event page (server component), read the cookie and render the PIN banner. Also, need to consume it so a refresh doesn't re-show it. Options:
>    - The page renders the PIN, and a small client component calls a server action `consumeAgentPinAction()` on mount that deletes the cookie. This is the cleanest — display once, then clear.
>    - Alternatively, redirect to a clean URL after reading — but redirect in server component render isn't great.
> 
> Let me do: page reads cookie, if present, renders banner AND a client component `PinReveal` that on mount calls `consumeRevealAction()` (server action that deletes the cookie). The PIN is passed as props to the client component? No — we can render the banner directly in the server component (it's fine; the PIN shows in HTML), and separately mount a tiny client component that clears the cookie. If JS disabled, cookie expires in 120s anyway.
> 
> Actually simpler: pass pin+name to a client component `AgentPinBanner` that renders and calls consume on mount. But rendering in server component is fine too. Let me keep the banner server-rendered (matches existing style, dark-mode classes etc.) and add a `PinRevealConsumer` client component (renders null) that calls the consume action on mount.
>

> Now I need to update the event page to read the reveal cookie instead of query params. The page currently reads:
> - `const agentPin = sp.agentPin ?? null;`
> - `const agentName = sp.agentName ? decodeURIComponent(sp.agentName) : null;`
> - `const terminalPin = sp.terminalPin ?? null;`
> - `const terminalName = sp.terminalName ? decodeURIComponent(sp.terminalName) : null;`

> And the banners use `agentPin && (...)`, `terminalPin && (...)`.
> 
> I need to:
> 1. Import `cookies` from `next/headers` in the page.
> 2. Read the reveal cookie and parse it.
> 3. Replace the banner conditions with the cookie-based values.
> 4. Add a client component that calls `consumeRevealAction` on mount so the cookie is cleared after display. Actually — since the cookie is httpOnly, the server reads it during render and displays the PIN. To ensure "displayed once", we should consume the cookie after the page renders. Options:
>    - A client component calls `consumeRevealAction()` on mount.
>    - Or redirect to a clean URL after reading... but a server component can't set/delete cookies during render (in Next 15+, `cookies().set/delete` only allowed in Server Actions / Route Handlers).
>    
>    So the cleanest: the server component reads the cookie and renders the PIN banner; a small client component (mounted once) calls `consumeRevealAction()` on mount to delete the cookie. If JS is disabled, the cookie expires after 2 minutes anyway. And the banner would show on refresh only if the cookie is still there — but since the consumer deletes it on mount, a refresh won't re-show it.
>

      import { randomInt } from "node:crypto";
      import { prisma } from "@/lib/prisma";
      import { TerminalStatus } from "@/app/generated/prisma/enums";
      
      // Durée de validité du code d'activation (15 min, cf. cahier des charges SIGMA Scanner).
      export const ACTIVATION_CODE_TTL_MS = 15 * 60_000;
      // Durée de validité du token d'authentification du terminal (renouvelé à chaque bootstrap).
      export const TERMINAL_TOKEN_TTL_MS = 12 * 3600_000;
      
      export function generateActivationCode(): string {
        return String(randomInt(0, 1_000_000)).padStart(6, "0");
      }
      
      export function generateTerminalToken(): string {
        return crypto.randomUUID().replace(/-/g, "") + crypto.randomUUID().replace(/-/g, "");
      }
      
      export function generateTerminalCode(): string {
        // Identifiant court du terminal, ex : T-9281 (lisible sur le dashboard).
        return `T-${randomInt(1000, 10000)}`;
      }
      
      type TerminalCreateInput = {
        eventId: string;
        name: string; // ex : "Porte A — Entrée principale"
        zone?: string | null; // ex : "main" | "vip" | "backstage"
      };
      
      // Crée un terminal INACTIVE avec un code d'activation temporaire.
      // L'organisateur le communique à l'agent qui le saisit dans SIGMA Scanner.
      export async function createTerminal({ eventId, name, zone }: TerminalCreateInput) {
        return prisma.terminal.create({
          data: {
            eventId,
            name,
            zone: zone || null,
            code: generateTerminalCode(),
            status: TerminalStatus.INACTIVE,
            activationCode: generateActivationCode(),
            activationCodeExpiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + ACTIVATION_CODE_TTL_MS),
          },
        });
      }
      
      // Génère un NOUVEAU code d'activation pour un terminal existant (l'ancien expire).
      export async function regenerateActivationCode(terminalId: string) {
        return prisma.terminal.update({
          where: { id: terminalId },
          data: {
            activationCode: generateActivationCode(),
            activationCodeExpiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + ACTIVATION_CODE_TTL_MS),
          },
        });
      }
      
      // Active un terminal avec le code d'activation saisi par l'agent :
      // associe terminal + événement + porte + agent, et émet un token court.
      export async function activateTerminalWithCode(code: string, agentId: string) {
        const terminal = await prisma.terminal.findFirst({
          where: {
            status: TerminalStatus.INACTIVE,
            activationCode: code.trim(),
            activationCodeExpiresAt: { gt: new Date() },
          },
        });
        if (!terminal) return null;
      
        const token = generateTerminalToken();
        return prisma.terminal.update({
          where: { id: terminal.id },
          data: {
            status: TerminalStatus.ACTIVE,
            agentId,
            token,
            tokenExpiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + TERMINAL_TOKEN_TTL_MS),
            activationCode: null, // le code ne sert plus qu'une fois
            activationCodeExpiresAt: null,
            lastSeenAt: new Date(),
          },
        });
      }
      
      // Authentifie un terminal par son token (Authorization: Bearer).
      export async function findTerminalByToken(token?: string | null) {
        if (!token) return null;
        const terminal = await prisma.terminal.findFirst({
          where: { token, tokenExpiresAt: { gt: new Date() } },
          include: { event: true, agent: true },
        });
        if (!terminal || terminal.status !== TerminalStatus.ACTIVE) return null;
        return terminal;
      }

### ⤷ Subagent: code-reviewer-deepseek-flash (code-reviewer-deepseek-flash)

_Prompt:_ Review these changes in sigma-security (Next.js 16, TypeScript):
1) lib/payments.ts: verifyWebhookSignature rewritten to Standard Webhooks spec — signed content = webhook-id + "." + webhook-timestamp + "." + rawBody (HMAC-SHA256), handles "v1," prefix, hex + base64 fallback, timing-safe compare, fallback to raw body alone when id/timestamp absent.
2) app/api/webhook/dodo/route.ts: reads webhook-id/webhook-timestamp/webhook-signature headers (with DODO_SIGNATURE_HEADER env override and fallback header names), parses payload.data.* fields (payment_id, status, total_amount in minor units), verifies paid amount matches order.amount + deliveryFee (either major or ×100 minor units), refuses with 409 AMOUNT_MISMATCH on mismatch, only confirms if status matches completed.
3) app/actions.ts: agent PIN and terminal activation code no longer passed via query string (security leak). New helpers stashRevealSecret()/consumeRevealAction() storing secret in httpOnly ephemeral cookie "sigma_reveal" (2 min TTL), redirects use flags like ?agentCreated=1, ?agentReset=1, ?terminalCreated=1, ?terminalRegenerated=1.
4) app/events/[id]/page.tsx: reads sigma_reveal cookie server-side, displays agent PIN / terminal activation code once, plus RevealConsumer client component that consumes (deletes) the cookie after display.
5) components/reveal-consumer.tsx: new client component calling consumeRevealAction() on mount.

Check for: security issues (cookie settings, timing attacks, amount comparison edge cases), TypeScript/Next.js correctness (cookies() usage in server actions, redirect after cookie set), regressions in the event page logic, and consistency with project conventions. Be critical and specific.

Let me review the changes critically. Let me think through each change.

1) `lib/payments.ts` — verifyWebhookSignature rewritten to Standard Webhooks spec.

Issues to consider:
- The signed content per Standard Webhooks is `id + "." + timestamp + "." + body`. Good.
- Handles "v1," prefix — good.
- hex + base64 fallback — the concern: `Buffer.from(provided, "hex")` — if the provided string isn't valid hex, Buffer.from will parse it partially (truncated) rather than throw. Then length comparison may fail → falls to base64. OK.
- One subtle bug: the base64 fallback only checks when hex length mismatch. But if the hex decode yields a buffer of the *same length* as expected by coincidence (unlikely for SHA256 = 32 bytes), timingSafeEqual would fail anyway. Fine.
- A real concern: for the base64 fallback path — `Buffer.from(provided, "base64")` is lenient and may decode garbage into some bytes; the length check protects. OK.
- Potential issue: `opts.signature` might include multiple signatures separated by spaces (some providers send multiple). Dodo/svix usually sends single. Could handle first token. Minor.
- The fallback to raw body alone when id/timestamp absent: that weakens security but maintains backward compat. Acceptable, though it means an attacker could potentially forge if they can craft raw body HMAC... no, the HMAC still requires the secret. Fine.

2) `app/api/webhook/dodo/route.ts`:
- Reads headers webhook-id/timestamp/signature with env override. Good.
- `signatureHeader()` — reads configured header first, then fallbacks. Fine.
- Parses payload.data.* with fallback to root fields. Good.
- Amount verification: `receivedMinor === expectedFcfa || receivedMinor === expectedFcfa * 100`.
  - Issue: The Dodo payment initiation sends `price: input.amount * 100` (minor units) in lib/payments.ts. The webhook receives total_amount in minor units presumably. The check accepts both. OK.
  - Edge case: `expectedFcfa * 100` — if `expectedFcfa` is 0 (free ticket?), Dodo wouldn't be used for free tickets (free tickets skip payment). But order.amount could be 0 in demo... Actually in real mode, orders with amount 0 skip. But what if amount is 0 and someone initiates? amount === 0 matches both. Minor.
  - Potential issue: `receivedRaw = Number(data.total_amount ?? ...)`. If total_amount is a string, Number() handles it. If NaN → amountMatches false → 409. Good.
  - Wait — there's a subtle bug: the check `receivedMinor === expectedFcfa * 100`. `expectedFcfa * 100` might be float if... no, amounts are ints. Fine.
  - One concern: **The `externalStatus` is set to `amount_mismatch` but no alert/log to organizer** — acceptable.
  - Bigger concern: **The webhook sets `externalStatus` but never updates `externalStatus` to "completed" after confirming**. Minor; not required.
  - Another concern: on AMOUNT_MISMATCH, it returns 409 — Dodo may retry. Fine.
  - Actually, a real issue: **`completed` detection uses `payload.type` including "succeeded"**. The event type for Dodo is `payment.succeeded`. Good. But what about `data.status` being "succeeded" — covered by regex. OK.

3) `app/actions.ts`:
- `stashRevealSecret` sets cookie httpOnly, sameSite lax, secure in prod, maxAge 2 min, path "/". 
  - **Issue: path "/" means the cookie is sent on all requests.** A 4-digit PIN in an httpOnly cookie sent to every path on the domain. It's better to scope path to `/events/${eventId}`. But the redirect target is `/events/${eventId}...` — scoping path to the event page would be more restrictive and better practice. However, cookie path matching: setting `path: /events/${eventId}` works for that page. This is a legit improvement.
  - **Issue: the cookie is not bound to the user.** An organizer who created an agent PIN gets a cookie. If they share a link? No — cookie is httpOnly, stays in browser. But there's a subtle issue: the cookie is set for the *current* user's browser, and the event page requires `requireUser(Role.ORGANIZER)` — so only an authenticated organizer viewing that event can see it. But nothing verifies the reveal cookie belongs to THIS event or THIS organizer. If an organizer has cookies for multiple events... only one "sigma_reveal" cookie (single key), so last write wins. If user creates an agent on event A, then quickly creates a terminal on event B, cookie is overwritten — the first reveal is lost. Edge case, acceptable but worth noting.
  - **Bigger security concern: the PIN is stored in plaintext in the cookie.** httpOnly protects from JS, but the PIN is the agent's password. It's displayed once. Standard practice (e.g., temporary tokens) is fine. The 2-min TTL limits exposure. Acceptable.
  - **Issue: `consumeRevealAction` deletes the cookie on mount of RevealConsumer.** The RevealConsumer is mounted on the event page. But the cookie is read server-side during page render — that's fine, cookie is read before the client component runs. However: **if the user reloads the page before the client JS runs** (slow network), cookie is still there, PIN shown again — but that's "again" only within 2 min and it was never deleted. Actually the flow: action sets cookie → redirect → page renders with PIN shown + RevealConsumer mounts → deletes cookie. If user hits refresh, cookie already deleted → PIN not shown again. Good. If user navigates away before JS runs... cookie persists until TTL. Minor.
  - **Potential real bug: Next.js server actions with `cookies()` — `store.set` then `redirect()`.** In Next.js, calling `redirect()` in a server action after setting cookies works — the cookie is set on the redirect response. This is the documented pattern (e.g., setting cookie then redirecting). OK.

Review of the changes:

**1. Webhook — false positive on payment status (most important).**
`const completed = /complete|success|paid/i.test(status) || String(payload.type ?? "").includes("succeeded");` — the regex matches the substring "paid" anywhere, so a status like `partially_paid` (or `unpaid`, `failed_payment`) is treated as **completed**, and the order gets confirmed without full payment. Use an exact whitelist instead:
```ts
const SUCCESS = new Set(["succeeded", "completed", "paid", "success"]);
const completed = SUCCESS.has(status.toLowerCase()) || String(payload.type ?? "").includes("succeeded");
```

**2. `stashRevealSecret` — unused `eventId` + cookie scope.**
`eventId` is passed but never used, and the cookie is set with `path: "/"`, so the agent PIN travels on *every* request to the domain for up to 2 minutes. Scope the cookie to the event page (`path: \`/events/${eventId}\``) — this uses the param and restricts exposure. It also fixes the multi-tab edge case where `RevealConsumer` on event B deletes the cookie before the user sees the PIN on event A.

**3. Page regression — reset shows "créé et assigné".**
After `resetAgentPinAction`, the banner renders the same text as creation ("Agent « X » créé et assigné"), which is misleading. The new redirect flags (`?agentCreated=1`, `?agentReset=1`, `?terminalCreated=1`, `?terminalRegenerated=1`) are written but **never read** by the page — dead params. Either read them to vary the banner text (e.g. "PIN réinitialisé"), or drop them.

**4. Minor.**
- The `v1,`-prefixed signature fallback logic is sound; no change needed.
- Cookie is not bound to a user/event beyond the session — acceptable given the 2-min TTL and organizer-only page, but worth a comment.
- Everything else (timing-safe compare, amount unit fallback, `cookies().set` → `redirect` pattern, try/catch around JSON parse, French comments) looks correct and consistent with project conventions.

Priorities: fix the status whitelist (#1), then scope the cookie and use `eventId` (#2), then correct the reset banner text via the existing flags (#3).

pas de repo git

// Secret éphémère affiché une seule fois (PIN agent / code d'activation terminal) :
// stocké dans un cookie httpOnly court (2 min), scopé au chemin de l'événement —
// jamais exposé dans l'historique, les logs serveur, ni sur d'autres pages.
const REVEAL_COOKIE = "sigma_reveal";
const REVEAL_TTL_S = 2 * 60;

async function stashRevealSecret(
  eventId: string,
  kind: "agentPin" | "terminalPin",
  secret: string,
  name: string
) {
  const store = await cookies();
  store.set(REVEAL_COOKIE, JSON.stringify({ kind, secret, name, eventId }), {
    httpOnly: true,
    sameSite: "lax",
    secure: process.env.NODE_ENV === "production",
    maxAge: REVEAL_TTL_S,
    // Le secret n'est envoyé que sur les pages de CET événement (et effacé sur
    // le même chemin) : il ne voyage pas sur tout le domaine.
    path: `/events/${eventId}`,
  });
}

// Consomme (efface) le secret éphémère après affichage par la page événement :
// un rechargement ne réaffiche jamais le PIN / code. L'effacement se fait sur le
// même chemin que la création (sinon le navigateur ne le supprime pas).
export async function consumeRevealAction() {
  const store = await cookies();
  const raw = store.get(REVEAL_COOKIE)?.value;
  let path = "/";
  if (raw) {
    try {
      const { eventId } = JSON.parse(raw) as { eventId?: string };
      if (eventId) path = `/events/${eventId}`;
    } catch {
      // Cookie invalide : effacement sur le chemin par défaut.
    }
  }
  // L'effacement doit cibler le même chemin que la création, sinon le navigateur
  // garde le cookie. (API Next.js : objet d'options avec `name`.)
  store.delete({ name: REVEAL_COOKIE, path });
}

// Crée un compte agent (ou réutilise un agent existant) et l'assigne à l'événement.
export async function addAgentAction(formData: FormData) {

/**
 * Vérifie la signature HMAC-SHA256 d'un webhook Dodo (spec Standard Webhooks,
 * docs.dodopayments.com/developer-resources/webhooks).
 *
 * Message signé : `webhook-id + "." + webhook-timestamp + "." + rawBody`
 * (le header `webhook-signature` peut être préfixé « v1, », format svix).
 *
 * Fallback : si `webhook-id`/`webhook-timestamp` sont absents (anciens webhooks),
 * on retombe sur le body brut seul. Comparaison à temps constant dans tous les cas.
 */
export function verifyWebhookSignature(
  rawBody: string,
  opts: { id?: string | null; timestamp?: string | null; signature?: string | null }
): boolean {
  const secret = process.env.DODO_WEBHOOK_SECRET;
  const signatureHeader = opts.signature;
  if (!secret || !signatureHeader) return false;
  try {
    // Spec Standard Webhooks : id.timestamp.body ; fallback = body seul.
    const signedContent =
      opts.id && opts.timestamp ? `${opts.id}.${opts.timestamp}.${rawBody}` : rawBody;
    const computed = crypto.createHmac("sha256", secret).update(signedContent).digest("hex");
    // La signature peut être « v1,<hex> » (svix) ou hex/base64 seule.
    const provided = signatureHeader.replace(/^v1[,;]?\s*/i, "").trim();
    const expected = Buffer.from(computed);
    const a = Buffer.from(provided, "hex");
    if (a.length !== expected.length) {
      // Fallback base64 (certains SDK encodent en base64).
      const b = Buffer.from(provided, "base64");
      if (b.length !== expected.length) return false;
      return crypto.timingSafeEqual(expected, b);
    }
    return crypto.timingSafeEqual(expected, a);
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

import { NextResponse } from "next/server";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

// Nom de l'en-tête de signature — configurable via DODO_SIGNATURE_HEADER.
// Dodo suit la spec Standard Webhooks : l'en-tête s'appelle « webhook-signature »
// (avec webhook-id + webhook-timestamp). Les autres noms sont des fallbacks
// pour les anciennes versions / proxys.
function signatureHeader(request: Request): string | null {
  const configured = process.env.DODO_SIGNATURE_HEADER;
  const candidates = [
    configured,
    "webhook-signature",
    "dodo-signature",
    "x-dodo-signature",
  ].filter(Boolean) as string[];
  for (const name of candidates) {
    const value = request.headers.get(name);
    if (value) return value;
  }
  return null;
}

// Webhook Dodo Payments : confirmation du paiement mobile money (HTTPS requis
// en production — la clé DODO_WEBHOOK_SECRET n'est jamais exposée).
//
// Flux réel :
//   1. /acheter/payer → initiation du paiement chez Dodo (lib/payments.ts)
//   2. le client paie sur le checkout Dodo (MTN MoMo / Moov / Orange / Celtiis)
//   3. Dodo POST /api/webhook/dodo (signature HMAC-SHA256 vérifiée ci-dessous)
//   4. la commande passe PAID, les billets QR sont émis, l'organisateur notifié
//
// Signature (spec Standard Webhooks) : HMAC-SHA256 de
// `webhook-id + "." + webhook-timestamp + "." + rawBody` avec DODO_WEBHOOK_SECRET.
// Payload : les données métier sont sous `data.*` (payment_id, status,
// total_amount en minor units — centimes pour une devise à 2 décimales).
export async function POST(request: Request) {
  // Le payload brut est nécessaire au HMAC : on le lit en texte.
  const rawBody = await request.text();
  const id = request.headers.get("webhook-id");
  const timestamp = request.headers.get("webhook-timestamp");
  const signature = signatureHeader(request);

  if (!verifyWebhookSignature(rawBody, { id, timestamp, signature })) {
    return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: "INVALID_SIGNATURE" }, { status: 401 });
  }

  let payload: Record<string, unknown>;
  try {
    payload = JSON.parse(rawBody) as Record<string, unknown>;
  } catch {
    return NextResponse.json({ ok: false, error: "INVALID_JSON" }, { status: 400 });
  }

## ✅ 3 points critiques corrigés & validés

### 1. Vérification du montant au webhook Dodo (`app/api/webhook/dodo/route.ts`)
- Lecture du payload selon la **spec Standard Webhooks** (`data.total_amount`, `data.status`, `data.payment_id`)
- **Refus `409 AMOUNT_MISMATCH`** si le montant reçu ≠ `amount + frais de livraison` (accepte l'unité majeure ou minor ×100) → un paiement partiel/surévalué n'est **jamais** confirmé
- Whitelist **exacte** des statuts de succès (`succeeded|completed|paid|success`) : `partially_paid` ne peut plus confirmer une commande (faille trouvée en revue)

### 2. Signature Dodo corrigée (`lib/payments.ts` + route)
La doc officielle révélait que le code était **incorrect** : le message signé n'est pas le body seul mais `webhook-id + "." + webhook-timestamp + "." + body` (HMAC-SHA256).
- Headers **`webhook-id` / `webhook-timestamp` / `webhook-signature`** (spec Standard Webhooks)
- Nouvelle env **`DODO_SIGNATURE_HEADER`** configurable (documentée dans `.env.example`) + fallbacks sur les anciens noms
- Gestion du préfixe `v1,` (format svix), encodage hex **et** base64, comparaison **timing-safe**, fallback body-seul pour compatibilité

### 3. PIN agent & code terminal sécurisés (`app/actions.ts`, `app/events/[id]/page.tsx`, `components/reveal-consumer.tsx`)
- **Fini le PIN dans l'URL** (`?agentPin=…` supprimé des 4 actions : addAgent, resetAgentPin, createTerminal, regenerateTerminalCode)
- Secret stocké dans un **cookie httpOnly éphémère** (TTL 2 min), **scopé au chemin `/events/<id>`** (ne voyage pas sur le domaine), effacé au même path après affichage → **affiché une seule fois**, invisible dans l'historique et les logs serveur
- Bandeaux différenciés : « Agent créé » vs « PIN réinitialisé », « Terminal créé » vs « Code régénéré »
